messages:
hannah: dropped a new prototype for the first-run helper. Two patterns: a thin persistent helper strip at bottom-right vs a pinned CTA at top of console. Which is less noisy for the checklist flow?

raj: my instinct is bottom-right helper strip. It stays out of the way but is visible. Top pinned CTA competes with our onboarding banner hierarchy.

emily: +1 strip, but need strong affordance for sample projects. Users often miss cards in the gallery. Can the strip collapse to a mini tray that expands into a small sample-project picker?

hannah: yep that's the idea. mini tray opens inline with a 3-card horizontal scroller. Each card has "Try with sample data" and a small toggle for telemetry (per project) — should that be per-project or global?

nate: per-project toggles are heavy. Keep privacy decisions global during onboarding; let advanced users toggle per-project later in settings. Simpler choice -> better completion.

emily: fair, but callout required: "Sample projects may send example requests for demos". Need to be explicit.

accessibility-bot: a11y notes on the strip: ensure keyboard focus path includes strip controls, aria-expanded on the tray, high-contrast focus ring, and role=dialog only when tray expands to avoid screen reader confusion.

hannah: good point. I'll add aria attributes: role=region + aria-label="Onboarding helper" on the strip, tray uses role=dialog when open and traps focus only while open.

raj: copy thoughts for strip label: currently "Try sample projects" vs "Explore sample projects". Which nudges more? I prefer "Explore" (less committal).

emily: "Explore" is nicer. Button microcopy on cards should be "Run with sample data" (verb-first).

nate: mobile layout: horizontal scroller turns into stacked cards. The strip becomes a floating FAB on small screens. Make sure it doesn't block primary CTA in the checklist.

hannah: noted. Also color contrast: current brand green on primary CTA is 3.8:1 on the strip icon — accessibility-bot flagged. Need AA contrast for normal text and 3:1 for large text. Swap to darker tint or add an outline.

accessibility-bot: confirm target: normal text >= 4.5:1, large text >= 3:1; focus ring min 3:1 against background. Also use visible focus indicators (not just box-shadow).

raj: performance: tray preloads sample project metadata on hover/interact so expand is instant. dev-bot: can we lazy-load code samples but fetch metadata earlier?

dev-bot: yes. Plan: fetch lightweight metadata on helper render (`/api/onboard/sample-metadata`) and lazy-load repo content or example payloads on first expand. Emit events: `onboard.helper_shown`, `onboard.sample_opened`, `onboard.sample_run`. Keep payloads minimal.

emily: analytics: track conversion from strip -> open -> run. We need to correlate with onboarding completion. Also capture whether user used sample projects vs creating own.

nate: small UX edge-case: if user closes the tray mid-run (they hit "Run with sample data" which provisions infra), show toast "Provisioning..." with link to view project. Provide a cancel button in the toast.

hannah: microcopy draft for tray header: "Sample projects to get started" with subtext "Prebuilt demos you can fork and run in seconds." Card body includes short bullets: language, model, expected latency.

raj: question: should sample projects consume free credits automatically? That could surprise users. Maybe show a small badge "Uses free credits" or require explicit confirmation on first run.

emily: show badge + confirmation modal on first run: "This demo will use X credits. Confirm?" keeps expectations set.

accessibility-bot: modal confirmation must be accessible: focus on dialog, Esc closes, return focus to triggering card button after close. Provide aria-describedby linking to explanation line.

hannah: decision proposal TL;DR: use persistent bottom-right helper strip -> expands to tray with 3-card scroller -> mobile uses FAB + stacked cards -> telemetry/global privacy choice at onboarding level (not per-card) -> sample project run requires one-time credits confirmation -> A11y checklist enforced.

raj: agree. Can we prototype the darker CTA and visible focus ring before the next design review?

emily: I'll push a quick color update and button states to the figma file and add examples of the toast lifecycle.

dev-bot: creating ticket INF-4302: onboard-helper, events schema, preload plan.

hannah: thanks all. I'll update the PR with screenshots and the accessibility checklist. Leaving a TODO to write microcopy for the credits confirmation modal. :sparkles:
